item.title: Control of Congress is at stake today. And, judge to consider motion in Clancy case
item.description: Election Day is here, and voters are heading to the polls in an election that may change control of Congress. And, a judge is considering whether to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case.

item.title: Death toll hits 29 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, with 48 still missing
item.description: Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, President Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections.

item.title: Haley Stevens backs Mike Rogers. And, Gulf states brace for potential attack on Iran
item.description: Democrats in Michigan are considering their options after Haley Stevens endorsed GOP candidate Mike Rogers for Senate. And the Gulf states are bracing for a possible U.S. attack on Iran after the midterms.

item.title: Hundreds evacuate city during temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
item.description: The ceasefire in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city has ended. The ceasefire, which lasted several days, allowed hundreds of residents to evacuate.

item.title: UN's peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ends after 35 years
item.description: The U.N.'s long-running peacekeeping mission for the disputed Western Sahara ceased operations Sunday after 35 years. Once ruled by Spain, it is claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front.

item.title: Gulf region on edge as Qatar leads talks with Iran to stave off new U.S. attacks
item.description: Qatar has been leading intense mediation efforts over the past 72 hours to prevent a new round of possible U.S. attacks on Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections. The uncertainty has the entire Gulf region on edge.

item.title: They signed up for a lifetime at sea on an endless cruise. High gas prices intervened
item.description: A cruise ship suspended operations suddenly, citing soaring fuel costs. Passengers, including Randy Cassingham, had to disembark in Cambodia. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Cassingham about the ordeal.

item.title: A new political era in the Southern Philippines
item.description: A new local government has taken its seat in the southern Philippines, in a step that marks a milestone in the peace process for a conflict that has lasted some 80 years.
